assessment.nobel_worthiness: A discernible change in the field: from proglucagon-derived GLP-1 biology and its insulinotropic, glucagonostatic and satiety actions to long-acting agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. The discovery is specific, original and has clear, lasting impact on physiology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its secretion and actions in humans), Drucker (mechanisms and preclinical-to-clinical translation of GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 form) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's pharmaceutical development of acylated analogues is also decisive for the therapies, and Habener-type early gene-structure work may not be in the supplied credit; the prize is capped at three, so this is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized outcome trials, and wide clinical adoption; recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Priority dispute over who first identified the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and whether basic-science versus drug-development credit should be split.
I have not independently verified details of the early peptide work; this rests on my general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsins as light-gated cation channels and their use to control genetically defined neurons with millisecond precision created a general experimental method that changed neuroscience and physiology. The importance and originality are very high, and the method redefined how circuits are tested causally.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann established channelrhodopsin function; Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck demonstrated neuronal control; six credited people exceed the cap. I would favor the channel discovery plus the neuronal-application breakthrough, but Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have strong claims and the choice is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over a decade and independently replicated everywhere; clinical translation (retinal optogenetics) is early, but the tool's impact is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel tradition of recognizing methods is best served by the channel discoverers or by the neuroscience users.
Allocation among six contributors is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new signaling pathway from the ER lumen to the nucleus, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and later PERK and ATF6 branches. It is conceptually clear, original and now central to understanding protein homeostasis in disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the two credited and make a coherent pair; the early yeast genetics (Walter, Mori) and the IRE1 mechanism are well documented. Others in the field (e.g., Ron, Kaufman) are not in the supplied credit, so the pair may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of independent confirmation; the pathway is textbook. Disease and therapeutic relevance continues to grow.
uncertainties: Whether the allocation should include figures outside the supplied credited names; I cannot assess them here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; this is a clear conceptual shift to living drugs, with substantial lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and genetic engineering of T cells), Sadelain (CD28-costimulated CAR design and preclinical proof) and June (clinical translation with 4-1BB CARs) is a defensible trio. Original CAR concepts by Eshhar and others are not in the supplied credit, which is a gap.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multiple independent clinical datasets; longer-term durability and expansion to solid tumours and autoimmunity are still being evaluated.
uncertainties: Priority claims by early CAR inventors outside the credited names.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancy, remains under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeting the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned CML from a fatal disease into a chronic condition and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy; a prototype with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (medicinal chemistry program) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a reasonable trio. Foundational work on the Philadelphia chromosome and ABL (Rowley, Nowell, Witte, Baltimore) is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of survival data and independent confirmation; recognition is clearly mature, so possibly overdue, but the field has been honored elsewhere.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would view this primarily as drug development (Lydon's work was industry-based) rather than discovery.
Foundational BCR-ABL discoveries by others are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide nusinersen corrected SMN2 splicing and gave a first effective disease-modifying treatment of spinal muscular atrophy; a clean mechanism-to-therapy story with a very large clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic splicing basis and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) is a natural pair. Others such as Hua and Rigo contributed and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016, with multi-year follow-up and independent trials; the broader antisense platform is still maturing, so some recognition may still be premature.
uncertainties: Whether a single therapy is enough for a prize versus the broader antisense concept.
Contribution of coworkers who are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR as the central regulator of growth and nutrient response links cell physiology to cancer, metabolism and ageing; the discovery has had broad, lasting conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Hall (identification of TOR genes in yeast) is the central figure. Sabatini (mTOR and mTORC1 regulation in mammalian cells) and Schreiber (FKBP12-rapamycin chemical biology) both contributed decisively but Sabatini's recent history may complicate recognition. Brown/Sabatini and Heitman-era yeast genetics are in some sense also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed over thirty years; therapeutic applications (rapalogs) are real though more limited than the biology.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit across the chemical-biology, yeast genetics and mammalian steps is debatable.
Conduct-related considerations about one credited person may affect a fair configuration; I am not asserting facts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified cytosolic DNA as a danger signal activating innate immunity through cGAMP, with importance for infection, autoimmunity and cancer immunotherapy; original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) is the decisive contributor; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING. Credited names also include Sun and Wu who worked in Chen's lab, so a trio of Chen, Barber and Ishikawa is plausible but the junior-author allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) has not yet produced approved drugs, so impact on medicine may be premature.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the STING and cGAS discoveries and the contributors in Chen's laboratory.
